validation.summary: 3 defect(s) detected. Structural score: 0.914. Coverage score: 1.000. Hallucination score: 1.000. Semantic score: 1.000. Overall score: 0.914.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers the main communication modes, optional encryption, and multicast group join/leave flows, but it still has a semantic termination issue for multicast and unicast/broadcast receipt flows. It also omits explicit decryption in the broadcast path, which is acceptable because broadcast requirements/scenario do not require encryption.

defects.description: The multicast receive path ends at N9 without a clear termination or continuation after satisfying the multicast scenario, while other branches explicitly terminate at N16. This creates an inconsistent completion flow for a required communication outcome.
defects.evidence: R19 requires that other agents in the multicast group receive the message. In the diagram, N8 -> N9 models sending and receiving multicast, but N9 has no outgoing edge, unlike N6 -> N7 -> N16 for encrypted/direct paths and N6 -> N16 for broadcast receipt.
defects.suggested_action: Connect N9 to the common end node or to the next explicit workflow step so the multicast receive path terminates consistently with the rest of the diagram.

defects.description: The broadcast receive path ends at N11 without a clear termination or continuation after satisfying the broadcast scenario, creating an inconsistent completion flow for a required communication outcome.
defects.evidence: R21 requires that other agents in the same local network receive the broadcast message. The diagram uses N10 -> N11 for broadcast, but N11 has no outgoing edge, while other branches continue to N16.
defects.suggested_action: Connect N11 to the common end node or to the next explicit workflow step so the broadcast receive path terminates consistently with the rest of the diagram.

strengths: Covers all three communication choices required by R4: unicast, multicast, and broadcast.
Includes join and leave multicast group actions and corresponding notify actions.
Models optional encryption via a decision node and separates encrypted vs. not encrypted paths.
Provides a decryption step for encrypted unicast/multicast flows, matching the secured communication requirements.
